brief: Double the X tweets: 8 multi-line X tweets (3 to 4 lines) and 4 single-line X tweets instead of the default 4 + 2. Make MOST of them (at least 2 of every 3) about Kaspa. Every Kaspa tweet still gets its IG companion per the default rule. Everything else at defaults.

fact_check.claim: 'the biggest single-day drop in the stock market like $3 trillion wiped out' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified: on Nov 5 2026 the S&P 500 lost around $3T (Reuters; Dow Jones Market Data ~$2.9T), the largest one-day dollar loss in its history; S&P -4.36% to 7,353.73. Not a record in percent terms, so copy says 'dollar drop' and dates it 'November 5'.

fact_check.claim: Selloff cause: AI regulation fears after the midterms (transcript links the Dems' AI stance to TAO)
fact_check.verdict: verified: Nasdaq-100 -~5.8% (~$1.9T), PHLX Semiconductor index -12%, on fears of an AI crackdown after Democrats won Congress. Copy says 'fear of an AI crackdown after the midterms', non-partisan. The TAO link is framed as Mike's opinion.

fact_check.claim: 'Bitcoin hanging in there above the 50-week moving average' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: UPDATED: the week from Oct 29 closed $80,441 vs a 50-week SMA of $75,979 (above); the week in progress (Kraken candle from Nov 5) is at $74,487 vs an SMA of $75,658, slightly under; CoinGecko spot $74,447. Copy says 'still fighting for its 50-week SMA around $75K', not 'above'.

fact_check.claim: 'I don't think there's gonna be a new bottom for Bitcoin below 57K'
fact_check.verdict: opinion; context verified: the 2026 low is July's ~$58.6K (CoinGecko). Copy: 'July's $58K low', 'I still don't see a new low under $57K'.

fact_check.claim: Kaspa below its 50-week SMA, good time to buy (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified: the KAS week from Oct 29 closed $0.03219 vs a 50-week SMA of $0.03555; the week in progress is at $0.02917 vs $0.03497 (~17% under). Spot $0.02914, market cap ~$810M; ATH $0.207 (Jul 2024), so ~86% under.

fact_check.claim: Kaspa stayed above its 50-week SMA from launch until December 2024 (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: accepted as Mike's chart read (the same claim is in the 2026-11-02 ledger); long-form copy keeps 'on my chart'.

fact_check.claim: '$100 trillion in crypto... Kaspa under a hundred billion... well above $3' and '$3.33 is going to be the start'
fact_check.verdict: math verified: circulating supply ~27.8B (CoinGecko market cap / price), so $100B = ~$3.60 a coin. The target is framed as Mike's prediction.

fact_check.claim: Kaspa is a PoW blockDAG at 10 blocks per second; mainnet November 2021; fair launch with no premine, presale or insider allocation
fact_check.verdict: verified: mainnet Nov 7 2021, fair launch, no premine; 10 BPS since the Crescendo hard fork (May 2025).

fact_check.claim: 'Silverscript is launched'
fact_check.verdict: verified: Silverscript v1.0.0 is tagged and live (covenant compiler); the Toccata hard fork activated 2026-06-30 per several outlets.

fact_check.claim: 'DagKnight... 100 blocks per second... targeted for a 2027 hard fork'
fact_check.verdict: partially verified: DagKnight is a planned consensus upgrade, not deployed; 100 BPS and the 2027 timing are roadmap projections. Copy says 'next on the roadmap... aimed at taking Kaspa from 10 toward 100 blocks per second', with NO date.

fact_check.claim: 'Kaspa sells speed to normies and war grade money to cypherpunks'
fact_check.verdict: a community line Mike endorsed on stream ('I approve of that'); used as his take, rephrased as 'hard money', no attribution or quote marks.

fact_check.claim: ETH flips BTC and Bitcoin maxis eventually move to Kaspa
fact_check.verdict: opinion; persona core thesis. Framed as 'it'll take years'.

fact_check.claim: JOLTS 7.5M vs 7.1M expected; ADP 86K vs 69K; initial claims 189K vs 196K; ISM PMI expansionary
fact_check.verdict: verified: JOLTS (September data, released Nov 3) 7.52M vs ~7.15M est; ADP 86K vs ~67K est (Schwab; Sigmanomics shows a 69K consensus); claims 189K vs 196K est. ISM PMI not checked independently, so not used.
fact_check.source: schwab.com weekly trader's outlook; sigmanomics.com; investing.com calendar

fact_check.claim: 'interest rates went up a month ago, only 25 basis points'
fact_check.verdict: verified: 25 bp hike in September 2026 (the first since July 2023); the October 28 FOMC held at 3.75-4.00%. Copy: 'hiked 25 basis points in September and held in October'.

fact_check.claim: QT ended and QE began; M2 is rising
fact_check.verdict: accepted as Mike's macro read (M2 chart shown on stream); copy stays general ('QE is running and M2 is rising again'), with no figures.

fact_check.claim: Fear & Greed down into fear
fact_check.verdict: verified: the alternative.me index read 29 (Fear) on 2026-11-09 and 25 (Extreme Fear) two days earlier.

fact_check.claim: The Clearing House partners with Quant on its On-Chain Money Initiative
fact_check.verdict: verified: announced 2026-09-24; Quant provides the interoperability / orchestration layer for TCH's tokenized-deposit network, live for participants in H1 2027. QNT is ~$202 now.

fact_check.claim: Base volume overtaking Solana
fact_check.verdict: UNVERIFIED (Mike could not find the source on stream); dropped.

fact_check.claim: Strait of Hormuz supply crunch
fact_check.verdict: Mike's macro read on stream; used once in YT post 2 as a general line with no figures and no war framing.

fact_check.claim: Skipped topics
fact_check.verdict: political tangents (Georgia recount, Epstein / JPMorgan), the IQ tangent, Naka / Hellhound gaming, Arrow, and the Linea / Canton deep-dive teasers: not drafted (persona avoid_in_drafts, off-thesis or unverified). No Zcash in this transcript.

yt_posts.topic: Kaspa under its 50-week SMA: born in a bull market, its first real bear market, the $100 trillion math, the DCA plan
yt_posts.body_style: reframe (first-ever bear market) then data walk then the plan
yt_posts.body:
Kaspa is on sale, and most people are too scared to notice. It just closed back under its 50-week SMA, the Fear & Greed Index is sitting in Fear, and the S&P 500 had the biggest one-day dollar drop in its history. But there's one thing about this Kaspa bear market that almost nobody is talking about, and it changes how I look at the whole chart.

Kaspa was born in a bull market. Mainnet went live in November 2021, and by the usual crypto definition (weekly closes above the 50-week SMA) it stayed in a bull market straight through 2022. Bitcoin was in a full bear market that whole year. Kaspa wasn't. On my chart, Kaspa only lost its 50-week SMA in December 2024.

So this is the first real bear market $KAS has ever had. Since December 2024 it has made a few attempts back above the line, a handful of weekly closes above it, then slipped back under. Right now it's around 2.9 cents, about 17% under the 50-week SMA and around 86% under its all-time high.

Think about what Bitcoin's first real bear market was. It was the best buy of its life. The people who sat through the boring part, the part where nobody wanted it, got paid.

Now the math. If crypto grows into a market the size of global stocks, you're talking around $100 trillion. In that world I can't imagine Kaspa under a $100 billion market cap. With around 27.8 billion coins out, that's well above $3 a coin. Kaspa is around an $810 million market cap right now. That's why I keep saying $3.33 is the start, not the ceiling.

And the chain isn't standing still. Silverscript is live, so smart contract logic can be written straight onto the L1. DagKnight is next on the roadmap, the consensus upgrade aimed at taking Kaspa from 10 blocks per second toward 100. Nothing about the chain got worse. Only the price got cheaper.

Here's how I'm playing it. I'm not trying to nail the exact bottom. If you have $200 to put in, put $100 in now and keep $100 for the next red week. If it drops, you buy cheaper. If it rips, at least you got half in. The next week or two could be red if the stock market keeps sliding, and I'm fine with that.

So where are you buying? Under 2 cents, right here, or are you waiting until it's back above the 50-week SMA? Tell me in the comments.

If this changed how you see the Kaspa chart, hit like and subscribe so you catch the next one before the crowd does.

yt_posts.topic: The S&P's record $3 trillion day versus Bitcoin: the trigger, the jobs data, the money supply, why this is not 2022
yt_posts.body_style: stat shock then three-part macro case then the risk line
yt_posts.body:
The S&P 500 lost around $3 trillion in a single session on November 5. That's the biggest one-day dollar drop in the index's history. And Bitcoin? It's still fighting for its 50-week SMA around $75K, nowhere near the $58K low it put in back in July. Here's why I don't think this turns into a 2022.

First, what actually happened. The S&P fell 4.36% that day, the Nasdaq-100 fell around 5.8%, and the chip stocks got hit hardest, down around 12%. The trigger wasn't a broken economy. It was fear of an AI crackdown after the midterms. That's a regulation scare, not a recession.

Second, the economy. Earlier this year my big worry was that there weren't enough new jobs being created, so if layoffs hit, nobody would get rehired. That's not where we are now. Job openings came in at 7.5 million against around 7.15 million expected. ADP came in at 86K against around 67K expected. Jobless claims came in at 189K against 196K expected. More jobs created, fewer jobs lost.

Third, the money. The money supply almost never shrinks. The big exception was 2022 into late 2023, when dollars were actually being destroyed, and that's exactly when crypto had its worst bear market. Now QE is running and M2 is climbing again. The Fed did hike 25 basis points in September and held in October, but one small hike doesn't undo more dollars in the system.

So my read: this drop has a lot more liquidity underneath it than the drops before it. The biggest wrench is still the supply squeeze around the Strait of Hormuz, which pushes prices up without being real money-supply inflation.

Here's the thing. If the S&P keeps sliding and we get a full 20% drawdown, Bitcoin probably doesn't hang in there. A real bear market in stocks drags everything down with it. But so far Bitcoin has held up much better than most people expected, and I still don't think it goes below $57K.

And notice the four-year cycle zombies moved the goalposts again. The bottom was supposed to be October. Now it's supposed to be a few weeks out because of the midterms. The cycle never set the bottom. Liquidity does.

So what do you think: does Bitcoin hold the 50-week SMA, retest July's $58K, or break to a new low? Tell me in the comments.

If this gave you a clearer read on the selloff, hit like and subscribe for more macro and crypto without the four-year cycle noise.
